subject: general
question: As of April 2025, which Ministry/Department approved 10 Plastic Parks in different states under the Scheme for Setting up of Plastic Parks in India?

options.text: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

solution:
The correct answer is __**Department of Chemicals and Petro-Chemicals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Department of Chemicals and Petro-Chemicals** under the **Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers** is responsible for formulating and implementing policies related to the chemical and petrochemical industry in India.
 
• The **Scheme for Setting up of Plastic Parks in India** aims to establish dedicated zones for plastic manufacturing and allied industries to improve infrastructure and boost domestic production.
 
• As of **April 2025**, the Department has approved the development of **10 Plastic Parks** in various states, such as Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, and Jharkhand, among others.
 
• The main objectives of these parks include promoting a cluster-based approach for the plastic industry, increasing competitiveness, and reducing environmental impact through proper waste management systems.
 
• The scheme encourages public-private partnerships (PPP) and provides financial assistance of up to **50% of the project cost**, subject to a ceiling of **Rs. 40 crore per project**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Plastic Parks Scheme:**

 
 
• The scheme was launched in **2013** by the Department of Chemicals and Petro-Chemicals to create state-of-the-art infrastructure for the plastic industry.
 
• Each Plastic Park spans an area of around **100 to 150 acres** and includes facilities like testing labs, training centers, and recycling units.
 
• The scheme aims to attract investments in the plastic sector and generate **employment opportunities**, especially in rural and semi-urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Department of Chemicals and Petro-Chemicals:**
 
 
• It is responsible for the development of the chemical and petrochemical sectors, which are crucial for industrial and economic growth.
 
• Key initiatives include the promotion of green chemistry, reduction of plastic waste, and support for the "Make in India" campaign in the chemical and plastic sectors.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Benefits:**
 
 
• Plastic Parks aim to minimize the **environmental impact** of plastic production by incorporating modern waste management techniques.
 
• Recycling units in these parks help reduce plastic waste and promote the circular economy.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Ministries:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** is involved in regulating environmental standards for plastic manufacturing and waste management.
 
• The **Department of Pharmaceuticals** oversees the use of plastics in medical and pharmaceutical applications, ensuring compliance with safety standards.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Plastic Industry in India:**

 
 
• India is the third-largest producer of plastic in the world, with the industry contributing significantly to the economy.
 
• The plastic industry supports various sectors such as packaging, healthcare, automotive, and construction.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Plastic Management:**
 
 
• India generates approximately **3.5 million tonnes** of plastic waste annually, with a low recycling rate of around **60%**.
 
• The Plastic Parks Scheme is a step towards addressing these challenges by promoting sustainable practices and advanced technologies.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Globally, countries like Germany and China have implemented similar industrial parks to support their plastic industries.
 
• India’s initiative aligns with international efforts to promote sustainable industrial growth and reduce plastic pollution.
